thread:
hannah: Hey all, quick onboarding Q. I'm wiring up a CI job to precompute embeddings for our docs using my hosted sandbox key. It runs fine on small samples but CI hits 429s halfway through a run. Error:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-type: token
retry-after: 45
```
I read that sandbox tokens have quotas; what's the recommended pattern for CI jobs? Do I ask infra for a different token, or should CI call a proxy?

infra-bot: FYI sandbox keys are intentionally rate and volume limited. Recommended CI patterns: 1) use a dedicated CI service account with a non-sandbox hosted token (ask infra for CI token provisioning); 2) push inputs to internal tmp S3 and run batch jobs from an ops account; or 3) request a short-lived temporary bump if this is a one-off.

leo: For recurring CI runs we usually provision a "ci-embeddings" token scoped to non-prod that has higher quotas. You'll need approval from infra + security. Open infra@redwood.com with subject "ci-token-request" and include repo, corp account id, expected monthly tokens, and owners.

hannah: Thanks. Is there an internal form for that, or email only? Also how long does approval take? We're trying to land this in our first-week demo pipeline.

devx-carmen: Email is fine, but there's also a Jira template linked in the onboarding docs (Search > infra requests). Approval time depends on load but typical is 1-2 business days. If you need same-day, file the ticket and DM me; I can nudge infra. Also make sure CI never prints tokens in logs.

ops-jules: If you want to ship the demo sooner, ops can run the full batch from a reserved account this weekend. Upload sanitized input to internal S3 (non-public, lifecycle 7d) and DM me the path + cost center. That avoids your sandbox quota entirely.

sec-omar: Security reminder: CI tokens must be stored in vault, not in repo or plain env. If data contains customer PII, redact before upload or mark the S3 object sensitive and we'll coordinate additional controls. Ephemeral tokens are logged and preferred for one-off runs.

hannah: Great, I'll file the Jira, email infra, and upload sanitized data as a backup for ops-run. Cost center: "docs-search-demo". Estimated total tokens for full run ~1.1M, peak ~10 qps, duration ~2h. Appreciate all the pointers! :pray:
